chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding the defamation, (to be) the reprimanding.
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed punishment for defamation in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) judicial discretion in applying ta'zir for defamation, reflecting the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence where penalties are tailored to the context rather than fixed. It underscores the principle that the judge (qadi) has the authority to determine the severity of the punishment based on the circumstances of the case. This ruling is foundational in understanding how discretionary penalties operate within the broader framework of Islamic criminal law.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding the defamation, (to be) the reprimanding’.
